claim: Bertrand's chord problem has no single answer from 'at random' alone: three uniform readings give 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, so the prior must be tied to the sampling process.
agent_test: Give the agent tasks with an under-specified 'random' and check it names the parameterisation before choosing a prior.
audit_note: Jaynes PDF unreadable via fetch; Wikipedia and Drory confirm. Note Jaynes himself argued invariance selects 1/2, so 'no single answer' holds only absent a specified sampling process.

claim: Jaynes's invariance argument (rotation, scale, translation) picks 1/2, but the same symmetry reasoning can support other answers; Drory's experiment (700 attempts, 363 successes, 123 chords longer than the triangle side, 0.339) fits 1/3 and not 1/2 for a different generating process.
agent_test: Not agent-testable directly; use as a rule: list the invariances, and accept that the list can be incomplete.

claim: Indifference is language-dependent: uniform in side, area or volume gives P=1/2, 1/4, 1/8 for the same event.
agent_test: Run the agent on a cube-style reparameterisation task with and without a forced 'flat over which variable' step.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: For an unknown pass rate, the choice among Haldane (1/(t(1-t))), Jeffreys Beta(1/2,1/2) and uniform Beta(1,1) changes early estimates (the rule of succession gives 4/5 after 3 successes under uniform). Jeffreys is the choice that is invariant under reparameterisation, but Jaynes argues for Haldane as the ignorance prior and Gelman, Simpson and Betancourt argue that no default is safe without checking its implications for the likelihood.
agent_test: Replay class records with 0-5 prior runs under the three priors; compare gate calibration (Brier) at equal tokens.
audit_note: Haldane/Jeffreys/uniform forms and 4/5 rule of succession check out, and Jeffreys is reparameterisation-invariant, but the sources do not support calling it 'the default': Jaynes 1968 argues for 1/(t(1-t)) for total ignorance and Gelman et al. say no default prior is safe independent of the likelihood.
claim_before_audit: For an unknown pass rate, the choice among Haldane (1/(t(1-t))), Jeffreys Beta(1/2,1/2) and uniform Beta(1,1) changes early estimates (rule of succession gives 4/5 after 3 successes under uniform); Jeffreys is the reparameterisation-safe default.

claim: Flat priors are not harmless with small data: with an 8 +/- 3.3 point estimate, a uniform prior gives 99.2% for a true effect, while a weakly informative prior N(0,0.005) gives posterior mean 0.002.
agent_test: Seed pure-noise tasks and check whether a history-based prior stops the agent from acting on noise.
audit_note: Minor: Gelman et al. posterior sd/99.2%/N(0,0.005) mean 0.002 verified in PDF text; the example concerns a sex-ratio survey and the claim omits that context.

claim: Shrinking thin per-unit records toward a pooled mean beats raw per-unit records: James-Stein total squared error .022 vs .077 (ratio 3.5) on 18 baseball players (re-verified in the paper text).
agent_test: Compare raw class pass rate versus pooled-shrunk rate on held-out runs for classes with n<10.
audit_note: Minor: .077 vs .022 and 3.5x verified in Efron-Morris text; claim generalises from one 18-player example, Chen and Lei support the general point qualitatively only.

claim: A prior needs an explicit strength (Carnap lambda, effective sample size, pseudo-counts); a single credence hides evidence quality (Keynes urns).
agent_test: Store k of n beside every class prior and test whether the gate with (k,n) beats the gate with a bare rate.
audit_note: Minor: Keynes urns and Carnap lambda confirmed in SEP; Selby abstract does not mention effective sample size (only the researcher's reading of the full text); 'needs' is a design recommendation, not a finding.

claim: Merging-of-opinions and self-correction guarantees are asymptotic; the SEP itself flags that the long run may be too long, so small-sample behaviour of the prior matters for an agent.
agent_test: Measure gate error as a function of class-record size (n=0,1,3,10,30).

claim: LLMs carry built-in priors that instructions do not override: base models put 60-80% on heads in coin flips; in-context evidence outweighs stated bias; scale (Pythia 70M-12B) did not fix it.
agent_test: Give the model a stated prior in words versus counts in context versus code-computed posterior; compare calibration.
audit_note: Minor: base-model 60-80% heads, Pythia 70M-12B no scale fix verified in Gupta et al. PDF; instruct models follow instructions slightly better, so 'instructions do not override' applies mainly to base models. Third listed source (MMLU label prior) is a different phenomenon.

claim: Given enough observations, in-context updating is close to Bayesian for small coin tasks, but in a multi-round recommendation task off-the-shelf LLMs plateau after round 1 (about 36-58% vs 81% for the Bayesian Assistant) and chain of thought did not help.
agent_test: Do updates in code on k/n counts, not in the model's head; test against model-only updating at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: plateau after round 1, CoT no help, and near-Bayesian coin updating verified; the 81% and 36-58% figures appear only in figures, not found in text (paper text puts original-LLM flight baseline at 37.0% and chance at 33.3%, not 37% chance as one note says).

claim: Fine-tuning on a Bayesian Assistant's outputs transfers (about 80% agreement) and beats fine-tuning on true labels; this is a training result, so out of scope for a scaffold-only agent.
agent_test: Not applicable (training); the scaffold analogue is a Bayesian helper in code.

claim: LLM base-rate use depends on the description: with an uncharacteristic description models use the base rate (odds ratio 9 for GPT-4o, GPT-4, Llama-3-70B; 8.86 Claude-3-Opus; 6.36 Gemini-1.5-Pro; 3 Mistral-Large; humans 2.25), with a stereotypical description ratios fall to 1.18-2.58 (re-verified).
agent_test: Insert the class record as an explicit numbered line before the case description and test whether it survives stereotypical case text.
audit_note: Minor: all odds ratios verified in Li and Rui; Talboy and Fuller (the second listed paper) is a mammography study and does not corroborate them, so the numbers rest on one paper.

claim: When the model must recall a base rate itself, its posterior tracks similarity to the field (Spearman 0.87-0.94) and runs against the true prior (-0.84 to -0.90); recalled priors are inconsistent (2-4% stated, 10-30% used).
agent_test: Supply base rates from a stored record instead of asking the model to recall them.
audit_note: Numbers verified in Li and Rui (0.87-0.94, -0.84 to -0.90, 2-4% vs 10-30% for GPT-4o); all listed Li-and-Rui entries are one paper and Scholten was not opened; GPT-4o only for the recall inconsistency.

claim: Wording of the task changes base-rate use more than reasoning instructions: 'indicate' to 'compute' raised GPT-4o ratio from about 1.25 to about 9.5, while four explicit Bayes-rule prompts did not fix the unstructured test.
agent_test: Ask for a computed posterior with named inputs versus a judgment; compare.

claim: Prompt-level debiasing for base-rate neglect is unreliable: CogBias prompt debiasing lowered judgment accuracy 4.4 points; in forecasting, 'reason Bayesian' worsened Brier by +0.025 (adj p 0.036) while Base Rate First improved it by -0.016 (adj p 0.036) and Frequency-Based Reasoning by -0.019 (adj p 0.022) (Schoenegger values re-verified).
agent_test: Test 'start from the stored class rate' against 'reason Bayesian' at equal tokens on forecasting-style items.
audit_note: Minor: CogBias -4.4 is the aggregate Judgment-family accuracy change over three models (Judgment includes a base-rate category); Schoenegger Brier values and adjusted p-values verified in PDF text; forecasting prompts are only loosely about base-rate neglect.

claim: Natural frequency formats raise correct Bayesian reasoning in humans (meta-analysis headline 24% vs 4%; Weber et al. about 36% vs 20%) but many students still convert to probabilities; benefit for LLMs is only second-hand.
agent_test: Present the class record as 'k of n' versus a percentage; compare agent use of the prior.

claim: LLM-elicited priors are model- and prompt-dependent and do not copy human experts: most centre Cohen's d at 0.2-0.25, GPT-4 near 0.5; Mistral-7B gave t(30) every time; some effective sample sizes above 1000.
agent_test: Never use a model-stated prior without an ESS check against data; compare two models' priors on the same task.

claim: LLM-stated priors often conflict with data: effective sample size near 0 (about 2) for weather quantities, and LLM imputation did not consistently beat mean/kNN/random forest.
agent_test: Score an LLM-guessed prior versus the class record on held-out outcomes.

claim: In Selby et al. (2025), given a single row, GPT-3.5 recognised 6 of 11 datasets, Gemini 1.5 Pro 5 and Llama 2 70B 2, so data leakage is a possible contaminant of tests of LLM prior knowledge (single study; inflation of scores not shown).
agent_test: Use private or post-cutoff tasks for any prior-elicitation test.
audit_note: Numbers 6/5/2 of 11 verified in Selby et al., but that is the only supporting paper (b19 and c07 are the same paper; AutoElicit does not address leakage), and dataset recognition shows possible contamination, not that scores were inflated.
claim_before_audit: Data leakage inflates tests of LLM prior knowledge: GPT-3.5 recognised 6 of 11 datasets from one row, Gemini 1.5 Pro 5, Llama 2 70B 2.

claim: Iterated-learning readout can recover GPT-4's implicit prior (100 chains x 12 iterations; convergence by iteration 7-8) and it resembles human priors in shape (U-shaped for coin proportions), though a uniform prior fits causal-strength judgments almost as well (r 0.85 vs 0.86 generative).
agent_test: Probe the agent's own prior on pass-rate questions and compare it with measured class records.

claim: LLM-elicited priors cut labelled data needed in linear-model tasks (AutoElicit: about 10x lower MSE after 5 examples on synthetic data, same peak accuracy 220 days earlier on UTI data), but weak models return uninformative priors and in-context predictions mismatch elicited priors.
agent_test: Run an LLM prior as a labelled alternative to the recorded prior; adopt only if prior-predictive scores beat it.

claim: The claim that LLM hyperpriors save about 66 patients is weak: one trial, one model setting; Llama 3.3 blind T=1.0 LPD -3.842 +/- 0.294 vs baseline -3.963 +/- 0.464, 80% data -4.093 +/- 0.107 vs 100% baseline -4.103 +/- 0.136, all within one SD; MedGemma T=0.5 was worse than baseline. (b21 and c10 are the same paper.)
agent_test: Treat as unconfirmed; do not rely on LLM-prior sample-saving claims without replication.

claim: Calibrating a model's prior alone raises its Bayesian error; calibrating prior plus rescaling the posterior reduces it (BASIL).
agent_test: Check stated-prior to stated-posterior consistency in the agent; fix by computing the posterior in code.

claim: Bayesian scaling laws (Arora et al. 2025) find that in toy models SFT mostly shifts the model's task prior rather than its task knowledge (DPO also disturbs task knowledge), and fitted parameters on Llama 3.1 8B Base vs Instruct are read as further, non-conclusive evidence of the same; Xie et al. (2022) frame in-context learning as implicit Bayesian inference over a pretraining mixture of latent concepts with a prior.
agent_test: Theoretical background; no direct test.
audit_note: Arora et al. find that on toy GPT-2/GINC models SFT mostly shifts the task prior while DPO also disrupts task knowledge; the real-model (Llama 3.1) evidence is inferred from fitted parameters and the authors say they do not claim LLMs are Bayesian learners; Xie et al. support only the in-context mixture framing.
claim_before_audit: Post-training mostly shifts the model's task prior, not task knowledge (Bayesian scaling laws); in-context learning can be framed as inference over a pretraining mixture with a prior.

claim: Models also carry a prior over answer labels: GPT-2 scored 0.007 on MMLU questions where A is never correct vs about 0.33 elsewhere; Mistral 0.273 (never A) vs 0.512 (never D).
agent_test: Shuffle option order and measure label-prior effect on the agent.

claim: LLM forecasting is near but below the crowd: system Brier 0.179 vs crowd 0.149, random 0.250, best zero-shot 0.208; retrieval helps (0.206 to 0.186).
agent_test: Compare an agent with and without retrieval of reference-class outcomes on dated forecast questions.

claim: LLM calibration is good on well-formatted multiple-choice but breaks out of distribution, so a model's self-stated probability is a weak prior for a new task class.
agent_test: Check calibration of agent confidence per task class before using it as a prior.

claim: LLM probabilistic judgments vary across runs and versions: mammography answers changed between March and August 2023; GPT-4 was correct with correct reasoning 69.2% and Claude 2 55.0% across 12 tasks.
agent_test: Repeat each base-rate item 10 times and report the spread.
audit_note: Minor: mammography change verified for ChatGPT-3.5 and Bard only (GPT-4 not tested in March); 69.2%/55.0% are accuracy rates over 12 tasks x 10 runs from Macmillan-Scott and Musolesi, which are not themselves a measure of drift.

claim: Shrinking a small class record (k of n, n<10) toward a prior beats raw k/n in synthetic tests: Brier 0.2339 (Beta(1,1)) vs 0.2678 (raw) at pool strength 6; a recalled prior that is 0.2 too high (0.2794) is worse than a flat 0.5 (0.250). Not yet tested on real run logs.
agent_test: Replay our run logs: compare Brier of raw k/n, Beta(1,1) shrinkage, pooled-EB and the model's own recalled prior, per class with n<10, at equal tokens.

claim: For a class with zero history, Beta(1,1), Jeffreys and Haldane give the same point value 0.5 or are unusable; only a pooled empirical prior moves it (Brier 0.240 vs 0.250 at pool mean 0.6 in simulation). Winkler et al. show that different 'noninformative' defaults give posterior 0.95 fractiles from near 0 up to 0.018 at n=167, 0 events.
agent_test: Check that the S0 gate uses the pooled rate for new classes and logs which default was used.

claim: Prior strength estimated by empirical Bayes across classes is unstable with few classes: in simulation (true strength 6) method-of-moments EB lost to fixed Beta(1,1) at 5 and 10 classes and won from about 20 classes (0.2324 vs 0.2345). Real-data support: Chen and Lei's shrinkage with data-tuned weight had the lowest holdout MSE in 3 of 3 datasets, with gains of about 1 to 5 percent.
agent_test: Fit strength on logs with 5, 10, 20, 50 classes by resampling, and compare to a fixed strength.

claim: An exact prior-predictive check exists for class records: the beta-binomial tail probability (Evans-Moshonov; Nott et al.). In simulation its false-alarm rate is at or below alpha (0.014 to 0.051 at alpha 0.05) and its power against a true rate 0.4 below the prior mean is only 0.33 to 0.38 at n=5 to 10.
agent_test: Run the check on logs: does a flagged case have lower accuracy than unflagged cases of the same class?

claim: Giving the model a raw list of outcomes to count is unreliable and sensitive to labels and order: accuracy at 54 labels falls to 0.21 (Llama3.1-8B) and 0.65 (Qwen2.5-7B); order changes next-token probabilities by 0.011 to 0.039 bits. A precomputed (k,n) in a fixed format avoids this. Direct LLM test of (k,n) vs bare percentage is still missing.
agent_test: A/B: bare percentage vs (k,n) vs (k,n,ESS) in the gate prompt; measure how often the model's final probability stays within 0.1 of the shrunk posterior.

claim: No evidence found that 2025-2026 reasoning models avoid similarity-over-base-rate behaviour. The newest LLM studies found (CogBias 2026, BayesBench 2026, Pournemat 2025) use GPT-4o-mini, Llama 3/3.3, Qwen 2.5 and a 7B R1 distill. BayesBench shows large models over-update toward 0 or 1 over 100 coin flips.
agent_test: Re-run the Li and Rui semi-structured probe on current models with and without a code-computed posterior.

claim: Conservative shading of an input prior can reverse a downstream decision: using a Rule-of-Three upper bound as the false-positive rate gave a diagnostic probability of 0.018 vs 0.053 from an informative Beta(1,999) prior.
agent_test: Pass the posterior mean, not a pessimistic bound, into gate arithmetic; test on a case where the sign flips.
